post_title: How many cumulative confirmed Ebola cases will the DRC's 2026 outbreak have reported as of October 31, 2026?

question.title: How many cumulative confirmed Ebola cases will the DRC's 2026 outbreak have reported as of October 31, 2026?
question.description:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has been battling its 17th Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), declared in 2026. It is by far the largest Ebola outbreak in the country's history and one of the largest ever recorded. The outbreak surpassed 1,000 confirmed cases within 40 days of response activation (versus roughly 235 days in the 2018 DRC outbreak).

Cumulative confirmed-case totals reported by the ECDC (which compiles DRC INSP data and updates every weekday) have climbed steadily:
- 6 October 2026: 8,728 confirmed cases, 4,205 deaths (WHO DON619)
- 12 October 2026: 9,144 confirmed cases (79 new cases reported on 12 October)
- 14 October 2026: about 9,277 confirmed cases, 4,478 deaths; 65 new confirmed cases reported on 14 October

Daily new-case counts have recently been on the order of roughly 60-80 per day, though with substantial day-to-day variation and the outbreak continuing to expand geographically (new cases in October concentrated in Ituri, North Kivu, and Haut-Uele, with North Ubangi newly reporting cases in mid-October). Response activities include MSF-run Ebola management centers; MSF reported admitting over 10,000 patients, of which about 5,200 were confirmed cases.

Projecting the cumulative total to the 31 October 2026 reporting date depends on whether daily incidence accelerates (continued geographic spread), holds steady, or slows (as response efforts mature). Province-level and national cumulative counts are published by the DRC's Institut National de Sante Publique (INSP) in daily situation reports and compiled by the ECDC on its outbreak page.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the cumulative number of laboratory-confirmed cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's 2026 Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak, as reported for the reporting date of 31 October 2026 (or, if that exact date is not available, the latest reporting date on or before 31 October 2026) in official situation reporting. The primary source is the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) outbreak page (https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/ebola-outbreak-democratic-republic-congo-and-uganda), which is updated every weekday and reports the DRC cumulative confirmed case total; the DRC INSP daily situation reports (https://insp.cd/category/sitrep/) or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used if the ECDC figure is unavailable. For example, a report of 10,250 confirmed cases resolves as 10250. Only confirmed cases (not suspected or probable) in the DRC count.
question.fine_print: The figure used is the cumulative DRC confirmed-case total attributed to the reporting date of 31 October 2026; because sources report on a lag, the value reflected for that reporting date in a report published in early November 2026 will be used. If no source reports a figure for any reporting date between 26 and 31 October 2026, resolution waits until such data is published. If the ECDC and INSP sources and all other credible sources permanently discontinue reporting this total before any figure for a reporting date on or after 26 October 2026 appears, the question is annulled. Figures for Uganda or any country other than the DRC are excluded.
